title: Pilot conflict triage deck & quickplays (draft)
body:
Status: working draft - rough speaker notes + quick scripts for SEs and field sellers.

Context and why this exists:
- We keep running into pilot conflicts: two internal teams or two customer use-cases that want reserved capacity/feature flags for the same window. SEs and AMs need a quick, defensible script to deconflict without losing momentum.
- This doc is a lightweight deck + pocket quickplays: 6 slides, 3 micro-scripts, and a 5-step triage checklist that field teams can use in live calls.

Target audience:
- SEs, sellers running pilots, platform/ops POCs, and CSMs.

TL;DR (elevator):
- 60s frame to calm the call: acknowledge, set constraints, propose an immediate win + long-term path.
- If capacity or SLA is the blocker, offer: (A) short-term hosted concession with token cap + audit trail, (B) canary on dedicated with throttles, (C) delayed start + prioritized ramp.

Deck outline (6 slides — keep visuals minimal):
1) One-line problem + urgency (1 min)
   - Visual: timeline heatmap (pilot overlap window highlighted)
2) 3 root causes (ops contended capacity, conflicting SLA expectations, overlapping feature rollouts)
3) Quick triage checklist (see below) + owner matrix
4) Recommended immediate plays (A/B/C with tradeoffs and scripts)
5) Risk reduction & rollback plan (canary metrics, rollback trigger thresholds)
6) Next steps + decision authority grid (who signs off, SLA delta sheet)

5-step triage checklist (use in first 5 minutes of escalation):
- 1) Confirm contract/commit: is there reserved capacity or signed SOW? (if yes → route to sales ops)
- 2) Confirm critical path: is pilot UX blocked or just degraded? (blocked → escalate faster)
- 3) Identify chokepoint: model variant, throughput, region, or feature flag?
- 4) Timebox a short fallback (30–120 min window): hosted fallback / model downgrade / burst quota
- 5) Assign owner + comms cadence (owner posts to #pilot-ops and opens JIRA PL-XXXX)

Three micro-scripts (pick-and-read):
- Script A (calm + close): "I hear you — overlap is real. Our immediate plan is to protect your SLA by offering a short canary window at lower throughput while we confirm capacity. Can I lock a 2-hour reserved burst and follow up with a rollback threshold we agree on?"
- Script B (commercial lever): "We can prioritize your ramp if you can sign the pilot amendment that adds a small reserved token pool for the first 30 days. That gives you predictability and lets us isolate impact."
- Script C (technical compromise): "If you can tolerate a 10–20% latency uptick for the first 48 hours, we can route low-priority traffic to an economical model variant and keep core requests on the baseline SLA model."

Recommended immediate plays (mapped to causes):
- Contended capacity → short-term: reserved burst for high-priority traffic + adaptive throttling. Long-term: schedule remediation and capacity commit.
- SLA mismatch → short-term: define measurable guardrails (p95 threshold, error-rate trigger); create shared dashboard link.
- Feature overlap → short-term: stagger feature flags by cohort; run A/B for 1 day.

Decision authority grid (who signs what):
- SE / AM: initial triage and offer script (can authorize 4-hour burst)
- Sales Ops: approves contract amendments (30d reserved pool)
- Platform Ops / SRE: approves model substitutions and region routing
- Product: approves any feature-flag gating that impacts experiment validity

Canary & rollback quick thresholds (example):
- Canary window: 2–4 hours for throughput checks
- Success: p95 latency < baseline+50ms, error-rate < baseline+0.5%
- Rollback: if p95 > baseline+120ms OR error-rate > baseline+1.5% for 10 mins → auto rollback and page on-call

Comms templates (short):
- Internal (to #pilot-ops): "Pilot triage: [customer] overlap with [other customer/feature]. Owner: @Liam. Proposed immediate play: 2-hour reserved burst at 50% capacity. Dashboard: <link>. Opening JIRA PL-XXXX."
- Customer update: "Thanks — we diagnosed an overlap during your ramp. We're doing a short controlled canary now and will share metrics in 2 hours. Your experience will be preserved; we'll follow up with the remediation plan."

Slide speaker notes (cheat lines):
- Slide 1: "This is a tactical deck — we want a decision in this call. I will propose 3 plays; pick one and we operationalize."
- Slide 4: "Tradeoffs: speed vs cost vs fidelity. Be explicit on which axis matters to the customer."

Open questions / TODOs:
- Pull in exact amendment language from legal for 30-day reserved pools (ping Legal: ticket LEG-88).
- Add a concise table of billing deltas for each play (ops to provide cost estimate).
- Validate rollback thresholds with SRE (SLO owners: @sofia).
- Create a one-click dashboard template (short link) to attach inside comms.

Related artifacts and where this sits:
- This is complementary to the 'pilot playbook' Confluence page (linked above) but lighter and designed for an SE live-call.
- We should convert the 6-slide outline into two versions: (a) two-slide 'fast decision' and (b) full 6-slide for follow-up.

Risks / guidance notes for SEs:
- Avoid promising capacity without Ops approval — use the exact phrasing in Script A to timebox offers.
- If a customer asks for on-prem/on-premise dedicated shifts mid-pilot, escalate to Solutions Eng immediately (long lead times).

Quick references (copyable snippets):
- JIRA template: "PL-XXXXX - pilot conflict triage for [customer]. Impact: [UX blocked/degraded]. Immediate play: [A/B/C]. Owner: [name]."
- Slack channel: #pilot-ops (post updates every 30m during active triage)

Notes to self:
- Iterate with Liam on cost table this week (need concrete $ delta for 2-hour burst on n1 vs n2 GPUs).
- Run a 1-hour dry-run with SEs (role play) before publishing to broader seller base.

-- end draft --

(very rough; intended to sit in Drive as an agile, changeable cheat-sheet. Will refine into slide deck and a one-pager.)
